citations.text: OpenEvo comparison of Pillow (2012), Barzilai and Chinn (2018, 2024) and Hanisch and Eirdosh (2023), 2026-11-18. A shared field concept proposed by the comparison; no source defines it.
Barzilai, S., & Chinn, C. A. (2018). On the goals of epistemic education: Promoting apt epistemic performance. Journal of the Learning Sciences, 27(3), 353-389.
Hanisch, S., & Eirdosh, D. (2023). Behavioral science and education for sustainable development: Towards metacognitive competency. Sustainability, 15(9), 7413.

en.general: Planning, directing and adjusting one's own thinking or behavior in light of what monitoring shows, for example choosing a different strategy, holding back a judgment, or changing what one does. Apt-AIR describes regulation of epistemic work: planning, monitoring, evaluating and controlling it. The Hanisch and Eirdosh design concept describes regulation of one's behavior. Pillow's book develops no regulation construct.

examples: A student switches from rereading to testing herself after noticing she does not remember.
A learner notices irritation, names it, and picks a response that fits what they value.
nonExamples: A habit that runs the same way whatever the feedback.
A rule imposed by someone else and followed without any check on whether it works.
